1.title: Infrastructure as Code and What Terraform Does
1.text: Welcome to Module one: Infrastructure as Code and What Terraform Does. It covers the exam area one. Infrastructure as Code. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. one A Explain what I A C is. one B Describe the advantages of I A C patterns. one C Explain how Terraform manages multi-cloud, hybrid cloud and service-agnostic workflows. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Infrastructure as Code with Terraform. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: What infrastructure as code is
1.text: What infrastructure as code is. Infrastructure as code means describing infrastructure in text files that a tool reads and applies, instead of clicking in a console or running one-off scripts.

1.title: What infrastructure as code is, continued
1.text: What infrastructure as code is. The figure shows this: Console clicks and scripts versus code that is reviewed, versioned and applied.

1.title: What infrastructure as code is, continued
1.text: What infrastructure as code is. Click in a console. Write configuration files. Hard to repeat. Repeatable in any environment. No history. Version control records every change. Drift nobody sees. The code is the documentation and the source of truth. Terraform is Hashi Corp's I A C tool. You write configuration in Hashi Corp Configuration Language (H C L) and Terraform creates, changes and destroys the infrastructure to match it. Declarative: you describe the desired end state ("three servers"), and Terraform works out the steps. An imperative script lists the steps itself. Exam tip: Terraform is declarative. You say what you want; Terraform decides how to get there.

1.title: Advantages of IaC patterns
1.text: Advantages of I A C patterns. Automation and speed. No manual steps; environments in minutes. Consistency and repeatability. The same code gives the same result; fewer configuration differences. Version control. History, review and rollback with Git. Collaboration. Teams review changes before they are applied. Reduced errors and risk. Fewer human mistakes; changes are previewed with a plan. Reusability. Modules share patterns across teams. Cost control. Create and destroy test environments on demand. Self-documentation. The files describe what exists.

1.title: Terraform workflow in one line
1.text: Terraform workflow in one line. Write the configuration to plan (preview the changes) to apply (make the changes). Details are in Module four.

1.title: Multi-cloud, hybrid cloud and service-agnostic
1.text: Multi-cloud, hybrid cloud and service-agnostic. Multi-cloud. Providers for A W S, Azure, Google Cloud and more; one workflow for all. Hybrid cloud. Providers for on-premises systems too (virtualization platforms, Kubernetes). Service-agnostic. A provider can wrap any A P I: D N S, monitoring, version control, sass. One language. H C L and the same commands everywhere. Terraform does not make the clouds the same: each provider's resource types differ. It gives one workflow, not one portable resource. Exam tip: Terraform manages infrastructure through providers, which talk to A P Is. The workflow is the same; the resource types are provider-specific.

1.title: Where Terraform fits
1.text: Where Terraform fits. Provisioning. Typical examples: Terraform. Focus: Create and manage infrastructure. Configuration management. Typical examples: Ansible, Chef, Puppet. Focus: Configure software on servers. Cloud-specific I A C. Typical examples: Cloud Formation, A R M (Azure Resource Manager) templates. Focus: One cloud. Exam tip: If a question says describe the end state, it is declarative (Terraform). If it lists the steps, it is imperative. I A C stores the source of truth in files.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team writes the desired number of servers in a file and lets the tool decide the steps. Which description fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A declarative approach, as Terraform uses. Terraform is declarative: you describe the desired end state and Terraform works out how to reach it.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company wants every change to its infrastructure to be reviewed in Git before it happens. Which I A C advantage is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Version control and collaboration. Storing the configuration in version control lets teams review, track and roll back changes.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. How does Terraform support working with several clouds? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: It uses providers and one common workflow. Providers talk to each A P I, and the write, plan and apply workflow is the same everywhere.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which statement about service-agnostic workflows is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Terraform can manage any service that offers an A P I through a provider. A provider can wrap any A P I, including D N S, monitoring or sass services.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which benefit does I A C give when a test environment must be built and removed every week? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Repeatable creation and destruction on demand. Because the environment is code, it can be created and destroyed repeatedly with the same result.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What is the language used to write Terraform configuration called? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Hashi Corp Configuration Language. Terraform configuration is written in Hashi Corp Configuration Language, H C L.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does I A C mean? Answer: Describing infrastructure in code that a tool applies. Question two. Is Terraform declarative or imperative? Answer: Declarative. Question three. Name two advantages of I A C. Answer: For example repeatability and version control.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What lets Terraform manage many platforms? Answer: Providers. Question five. What is H C L? Answer: The Hashi Corp Configuration Language. Question six. Does Terraform make all clouds use the same resource types? Answer: No, resource types are provider-specific.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. I A C: infrastructure described in files; code is the source of truth. Terraform: declarative, H C L, providers, plan then apply. Advantages: automation, consistency, version control, collaboration, fewer errors, reuse, cost. Scope: multi-cloud, hybrid, any A P I; one workflow, provider-specific resources.
